amana.notes: Building Center Amana page is history-only (https://www.building-center.org/amana-hvac-age/, no serial system), so these styles come from Amana-specific independent sources, NOT inherited from Goodman (usesStylesOf is null; the Goodman file is not cited as source): PickHVAC Amana page (primary), corroborated by GGR Home Inspections Amana guide and HowToLookAtAHouse Amana posts (first two digits = year) and an InterNACHI thread (9108033656 = August 1991, year-first/second-two-month). CONFLICT FLAGGED: QualityHomeAirCare states the opposite order (MMYY, example 0215 = February 2015) for Goodman & Amana; that source is the outlier against PickHVAC, GGR, HowToLookAtAHouse, InterNACHI, and the Building Center Goodman rule (YYMM), and its example contains a letter, inconsistent with all-numeric Amana serials, so YYMM is used. AUTHORITY NOTE: PickHVAC is a third-party decoder site, not manufacturer documentation; Fred approved keeping this file on Oct 28, 2026 on the strength of the 4-to-1 corroboration (PickHVAC + GGR + HowToLookAtAHouse + InterNACHI against the MMYY outlier). yearFloor 2001 on styles 1-2 reflects the sources' stated 2001-present era.

styles.notes: PickHVAC Style 1 example 0211847363 = November 2002; plate example 1612117501 = December 2016 (shown on the Amana page as a Goodman plate illustrating the same system).
PickHVAC Style 2 example 080359478 = March 2008. Source states the 9- vs 10-character difference is unclear; first four digits carry the date in both.

PickHVAC Style 3 example 98-90558 = 1998, month not encoded. Pattern is the normalized form: the builder strips dashes, so the documented 8-character 98-90558 becomes 7 digits; no undashed 7-digit Amana style is documented, so collision risk is noted but low.

american-standard.notes: Reuse evidence comes from the Trane page, NOT from this page: the Trane page labels the year-first system as a Trane (American Standard) style begun in 2002, states it remains in use under the Trane, American Standard, Ameristar and Ingersoll Rand names, and states the older styles continued in use for many years under the Ingersoll Rand, American Standard, Trane and GE names. CAVEAT: the American Standard page itself contains history only and no serial-number decoding section, so sister-page confirmation is unavailable; if the project requires sister-page confirmation strictly, hold this file as a gap instead of shipping reuse. No parent company is stated on the American Standard page, so parent is omitted.

styles.notes: Year-prefix range 10-26 in the pattern must be extended as the calendar advances; the century rule alone would misread pre-2010 digit-led serials. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2010+ reading) and style-1 (2002-2009 reading); this style is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading. The page notes the styles overlap and directs techs to the data-plate MFR date to disambiguate; a 2002 serial in the overlap set will decode as a 2020s year.

Single-digit year encoded as a digit-keyed letterTable because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the mapping (digit d = 2000+d for 2002-2009) is the page's stated rule. CAVEAT: the page notes some circa 1978-79 models may have used this shape, so a leading 8 or 9 could be 1978/1979 on a very old unit; condition and appearance disambiguate per the page. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2002-2009 reading) and style-2 (2010+ reading); style-2 is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading and the data-plate MFR date must disambiguate per the page. A 2002 serial in the overlap set therefore decodes as a 2020s year; this is a documented page ambiguity, not a silent guess.

Letter table: the page's chart is an image that text fetch cannot OCR. Anchors confirmed in page text: S = 1986, Z = 2001, F = 1991 (page example F23456789, 23rd week of 1991), C = 1988 (page example C01D47415, 1st week of 1988); header examples are consistent with R = 2000 and M = 1997. Remaining mappings corroborated by independent published Trane charts. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: page text says letters A, I, L, O and Q were not used, yet the standard chart reading (corroborated by three independent sources) gives L = 1996; L = 1996 is included pending visual chart verification. The page warns this style is easily confused with page styles 3, 4, 6 and 7.

styles.era: 1970s onward, factory letter + 2-digit year + month letter, 9 characters (page Style 3)
styles.notes: Page states the 4th position encodes month but gives no letter-to-month table (the documented example's 4th character is M), so month is not encoded. The page warns this style is easily confused with page Style 2; ordering (letter-year style tried first) plus week-range validation resolves most collisions, since a page-Style-3 serial whose factory letter is in the year table and whose year digits are 01-53 would otherwise decode as a letter-year serial.

bosch.notes: Single decodable style (page Styles 1a-1d, one shared system): 4-character Production/Plant Code, then the 3-character Manufacture Date code at normalized positions 5-7 (1-based) / [4,7] 0-based half-open, then Production Run Number and Part Number. The page states the date is always the 5th-7th characters regardless of dash locations or omission, and the four page sample serials confirm this on the normalized (dash-stripped) serial: each yields a chart code. Chart transcribed firsthand from the page's chart image (Bosch-date-chart-1.jpg, 1173x1054) on 2026-10-28; all 252 cells legible in enlarged bands, no cell guessed; 21 year-rows (2010-2030) x 12 months, every (year, month) pair covered exactly once. Chart quirks transcribed as printed, not smoothed: 2010-2013 run sequentially (e.g. 2013: 301-312), but 2014-2029 split each year into Jan-Apr (?17-?20) and May-Dec (?53-?60) with a jump between April and May (e.g. 2014: Apr 420, May 453); 2030 switches to alphanumeric codes 0A1-0AC. Page Styles 2 (63036333-00-7080-3241) and 3 (253000-08217-01241-7747019703) are HELD, NOT SHIPPED: the page states it cannot determine the year for either; both are pre-2010 legacy systems. Page header names related brands Bosch, Buderus, FHP, Chromalox, Worcester and parent Bosch Thermotechnology Corp. (described as a subsidiary of Advanced Thermal Technologies), but the page does not document those brands sharing this code system, so no sisters are claimed. Example decodes are derived, not stated on the page: the page gives the sample serials and the chart but no worked year/month for them; each expected value below is the chart entry for that serial's 5th-7th code, verified against the chart image.

styles.notes: codeTable supplies both year and month from the single 3-character code at normalized positions [4,7]; year/month fields are null because no separate year or month slice exists. Pattern length floor (22) is the shortest documented sample (Style 1b, 22 normalized characters); the other samples are 23. It excludes page Style 2 (18 normalized characters) and page Style 3 passes the pattern but its code '000' is not in the table, so it correctly yields no match rather than a guessed date. Codes are uppercase after normalization; the 2030 codes contain the letter A (0A1-0AC), so the code slice must not be restricted to digits.

bryant.notes: BDP system. Sister Payne shares styles 1-4 in shape, positions, era, and example serials. The page also lists Aquazone, BDP, Day and Night, and Weathermaster as related brands, but their serial systems were not verified in this batch and are not claimed as shared. Carrier is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not claimed as sharing this system. Style 3 Canada reverses year/month positions vs US. Single-digit years in styles 3, 3-Canada, and 4 are encoded as digit-keyed letterTable maps because the schema digits kind does not support 1-character year slices; the mappings themselves are fully documented on the page. Schema-prose note: the locked schema says letterTable keys must be single uppercase letters; digit keys work in the builder (JSON keys are strings, table lookup is exact) but a future schema clarification (digitTable kind or prose update) should ratify this.

styles.era: 10-character format, week-year in first four digits
styles.notes: Week is 1st-2nd positions, year is 3rd-4th positions. Week decode for the example is 07.
Year is 1st-2nd positions, month is 3rd-4th positions.

Month letter is 1st position, M-Z skipping O and U for January-December. Year digit is 2nd position, 0-4 for 1980-1984. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.
Canadian variant only: year digit is 1st position, month letter is 2nd position, same tables as US style 3. Split from style 3 because one style cannot carry two position assignments.

Month letter is 1st position, A-L with no letters skipped. Year digit is 2nd position, 0-9 for 1970-1979. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

Year letter begins with L for 1960 and cycles to H for 1979, skipping O, Q, and Z. Week is the 1st-2nd positions; the example week is 46. Split from the one-digit-week variant because fixed position ranges cannot express both.
Same year-letter table as style 5a. Week is the 1st position only; the example week is 2.

carrier.notes: Building Center Carrier page is history-only (https://www.building-center.org/carrier-hvac-age/, no serial system). Modern style is documented INDEPENDENTLY of Bryant/Payne files, in Carrier manufacturer documentation (brandportal product literature, serial-number nomenclature figure, repeated across 38AX, 38AU and 40RU documents): positions 1-2 = week of manufacture (fiscal calendar), 3-4 = year, 5 = manufacturing location, 6-10 = sequence number. Corroborated for residential equipment by Carrier Northwest (Carrier dealer site, example 5220 = 52nd week 2020) and SmartACSolutions (2714 = week 27 of 2014, mid-1990s to today). SCOPE CAVEAT: manufacturer documents cover commercial lines 38AX/38AU/40RU; the WWYY rule is corroborated, not manufacturer-proven, for residential lines. Older Carrier systems (1960s single-digit year, 1970s letter+digit, per inspector-training source only) are HELD, not drafted: incomplete and single-sourced. Week is a fiscal-calendar week per the manufacturer figure, not necessarily ISO week; recorded as week, as in Bryant/Payne files. Carrier derivation from Bryant/Payne was NOT used: no Bryant/Payne file content is cited as the source for this file.

styles.notes: Examples are the typical serials printed in the manufacturer nomenclature figures: 0525... = week 05, 2025 (38AXQ doc); 2623G12345 = week 26, 2023 (40RU doc); 0524... = week 05, 2024 (38AX doc). Position 5 is a location code (digit 9 in the 38AX typicals, letter G in the 40RU typical), hence [A-Z0-9].

coleman.notes: Coleman does NOT use usesStylesOf york: styles 1-2 match York's systems verbatim (same sample serials, same letter tables, same October 2004 boundary, charts note York UPG manufacturing), but styles 3-4 are Coleman-only numeric systems and the builder forbids styles alongside usesStylesOf. The month/year order swap is documented as a 1991/1992 boundary, not April 1992: style 4 (month first) ended 1991, style 3 (year first) began 1992. Dual-brand Coleman-Evcon history 1999-2005 is documented on the page. SHIPPED IN PHASE 2b: style-2 (1971 to October 2004, 4 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample WAKM011379 = January 1980 or 2001) via the dual-candidate schema extension; TEXT-SOURCED (see style-2 notes), Building Center chart image read still open. STILL HELD: style-1 (after October 2004, 10-character serials, sample W0K5896070 = September 2005) — the split-year schema blocker is gone in Phase 2b, but the style is held pending the Coleman chart image read (see image-pass report); it is NOT extrapolated from York here.

styles.notes: TEXT-SOURCED (Phase 2b, not Coleman-page image-verified): tables from York-family text decoders (PickHVAC, InterNACHI, Coleman decoder PDF), all agreeing, and identical to the shipped York style-2 tables; example serial is the Coleman page's own example. Month is 2nd letter, year is 3rd letter; I, O, Q, U, Z not used. Year codes repeat on a 21-year cycle, hence dual candidates. N=2004 is January-September 2004 only (post-2004 system from October 2004) — recorded here, not expressible in the table. K=September here is the OLD-system value and must not be carried into post-2004 style 1. Building Center chart image read still open for image confirmation.

Year first, month second. yearFloor 1992 reflects the documented start year; with this floor, trying style-3 before style-4 resolves the numeric overlap: a 9-digit serial whose style-3 month field is invalid falls through to style-4, and a serial matching style-3 with year 1992 or later cannot be a style-4 serial (style-4 ended 1991).

Month first, year second: the reverse of style-3. DOCUMENTED-LENGTH DISCREPANCY: the page's style list shows a 9-digit sample (018812345) but the style-4 chart body shows 10 digits (0188123456, month 01, year 88, 6-digit sequence); the 10-digit body serial is used as the example and the pattern allows 9-10 digits. RESIDUAL EDGE, flagged not resolved: a 9-digit serial that fails style-3 month validation but passes style-4 with a year of 1992 or later would decode to a post-1991 year outside style-4's documented era; the schema has no era upper bound to reject it. No start date is documented for this style, so the default 1960 floor is kept.

daikin.notes: Only 3 of the page's 10 styles encode as deterministic serial rules from the page text: page styles 2, 7 and 10. Page style 1 carries no serial encoding (year and month read only from the printed manufacture-date label) and is not encoded. Page styles 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 decode through charts shown only as images on the page; the chart contents are not recoverable from the page text, so no tables are encoded for them and they are held as gaps pending a read of the chart images. Related brands Goodman, Amana and Janitrol are listed on the page but use their own serial systems; no styles are copied from them and usesStylesOf is null. Two-digit years resolve by the schema century rule with floor 1960. Example decodes are derived mechanically from the page's documented positions (the page states positions, not manufactured-in sentences, for these three styles).

styles.era: Page style 2: 4-letter prefix followed by 10 digits
styles.notes: Page style 2: year is the 5th and 6th characters (first two digits after the 4-letter prefix), month is the 7th and 8th characters. Example decode derived from the documented positions: 09 -> 2009, 05 -> May.

styles.era: Page style 7: 1 letter followed by 9 digits
styles.notes: Page style 7: year is the 2nd and 3rd digits, week is the 4th and 5th digits. Example decode derived from the documented positions: 88 -> 1988, week 12.
Page style 10: year is the 1st and 2nd numbers, month is the 3rd and 4th numbers. Example decode derived from the documented positions: 16 -> 2016, 02 -> February.

goodman.notes: Style 1 is the 10-digit numeric system (fully validated). Style 2 (select PTAC systems manufactured for Goodman by Daikin Industries, serials ending in P or D, ended shortly after the 2012 Daikin acquisition) is NOT encoded: the page documents its letter positions (year = 3rd position / 2nd letter, month = 2nd position / 1st letter) and its example serial 5FU5472618P, but gives no letter-to-year or letter-to-month mapping in retrievable text and no stated decode for that example, so no Style 2 table is shipped rather than guessed. Amana is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not listed as a sister sharing this system and has no file (documented gap). The style list variant 9704 011000 shares Style 1's YYMM prefix but has no separately stated decode, so it is not added as an example.

styles.notes: Page positions 1-2 = year, 3-4 = month (1-based), converted to 0-based half-open ranges. Page example shown as 97 04811080.

janitrol.notes: Legacy brand: acquired by Goodman circa 1982, brand name discontinued in 1992; kept as its own file per the legacy pass-through rule, not merged into Goodman. Reuse evidence is page-framing only: the Janitrol page is headed Janitrol-Goodman-GmC-Amana and frames age determination as Goodman Manufacturing brand systems, with Goodman Manufacturing Company, L.P. as parent. The page gives no Janitrol-specific positions, formats, or examples, so this reuse rests on that framing, not on position-level confirmation on the Janitrol page.

styles.notes: Page positions 1-2 = year, 3-4 = month (1-based), converted to 0-based half-open ranges. Page example shown as 97 04811080.

keeprite.notes: ICP system. Styles 1-3 are identical to Tempstar styles 1-3 in example serials, shapes, and positions. NOT usesStylesOf Tempstar because Tempstar lists an additional style 6 that the Keeprite page does not list; verbatim reuse would add an unverified style to Keeprite. HELD GAPS — style 4 (8-digit numeric, year = 1st digit, week = 2nd-3rd digits): format example only, year mapping chart-image-only; style 5 (letter-digit-letter prefix, year = 3rd letter): placeholder only, year-letter chart image-only, tail shape undocumented. Neither is shipped rather than guessed.

styles.notes: Year is 2nd-3rd digits, week is 4th-5th digits. Week decode for the example is 16.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits, with printed MFG date on tag
styles.notes: Page states this serial is identical in system to style 1; the printed MFG date 2/92 corroborates year 1992 and week 06. Pattern and positions duplicate style 1, so this style never wins first-match, but its decode is identical.

styles.era: 10-character format, year-week in first four digits
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd digits, week is 3rd-4th digits. Week decode for the example is 14.

lennox.notes: Page lists related brands (AirEase, Airease-Johnson, Aire-flo, Allied-Commercial, Allied, Armstrong Air, Concord, Ducane, Magic-Pak, Advanced Distributor Products (ADP), Heatcraft) but does not document that any shares this serial system, so no sisters or usesStylesOf are set. Page presents pre-1973 serials as a single style with a 1- or 2-digit month; split here into two file styles because schema positions are fixed ranges. Two-digit years resolve by the schema century rule with the default 1960 floor, so pre-1960 pre-1973 serials return cannot-determine rather than a guessed year. The page documents only one month-letter system (A-M minus I, 1973+); there are no separate month-letter eras to encode.

lg.notes: Style 2 (EQ style) SHIPPABLE from the page diagram, which governs over the page body text: the body text positions (year 6th-10th, month 11th, day 12th-13th) give an impossible date (year 20013, month 5, day 00) for the diagram sample, while the diagram boxes give a valid date. Diagram (LG-2-Serial-Number.jpg): buyer code EQ (1-2), model code 11 (3-4), line number 2 (5), production year 2001 (6-9), production month 3 (10), day 15 (11-12), serial 0001 (13-16). The schema has no day field, so the day is recorded in notes only. The page section for this style is mislabelled Style 1 a second time; it is the EQ style listed as Style 2 at the top of the page. The page states this style is believed no longer in use. Style 1 (digit-led) is NOT shipped: year is a single digit with no page-stated decade bound — digit 4 is documented as 2004 (diagram sample 404KAPB00104), 2014 and 2024 (page text on 407HAVN79423, plate confirms 2024), and digit 2 as 2012 (plate 207KRMK0Y171, MANUFACTURED 2012.07) — so a two-candidate [2014, 2024] table for digit 4 is disproven, and an assumed 2000-2026 multi-candidate bound was rejected as assumed, not page-stated. Style 1 month (positions 2-3) is exact but year-decade-unknown; check the separate serial tag, which often carries the manufacture date on newer systems. Unresolved diagram anomaly, NOT encoded: the Style 1 diagram also claims 1201KAPB00104 = January 2012 with a 4-character date code, contradicting the current rule (positions 1 = year digit, 2-3 = month); such a serial correctly fails under the current rule.

styles.era: EQ style, believed no longer in use (page diagram)
styles.notes: Diagram sample EQ11220013150001 decodes to 2001-03-15 (year 2001, month 3, day 15). Page body-text positions are off by one and are NOT used; diagram governs.

luxaire.notes: Luxaire does NOT use usesStylesOf york: it has extra numeric and 2-letter styles, and its style-1 month table conflicts with York's for September-December (see held-style note). SHIPPED IN PHASE 2b: style-4 (4 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample WAKM011379 = January 1980 or 2001) via the dual-candidate schema extension; TEXT-SOURCED (see style-4 notes), Building Center chart image read still open. STILL HELD: style-1 (10-character serials, sample W0K5896070) — the split-year schema blocker is gone in Phase 2b, but the MONTH-TABLE CONFLICT blocks it: Luxaire's own style-1 chart maps K to October (J September, L November, M December, no N), while the York and Coleman charts map the same sample serial's K to September (K September, L October, M November, N December) — the same serial decodes to September 2005 on York/Coleman but October 2005 on Luxaire, and only a real data-plate/chart read can settle it, so Luxaire's table must not be overwritten with York's on suspicion. Style-4's month table (K September) also contradicts Luxaire's own style-1 table (K October); the plausible reading is two different systems' tables, not one contradiction — but style 1 itself stays held. Style-5 (2 letters + 6-digit sequence, sample HM409295 = August 1982 or 2003) is likewise held: no text table found for this 2-letter system and it must not be assumed identical to style 4's tables. Style-6 (11-digit numeric, year/month stated Unknown on the page) is intentionally omitted: no year can be extracted from it, and the page only gives a 1965-1981 company-name window and a contact-the-manufacturer instruction. Luxaire page last updated 2016, older than the York (2024) and Coleman (2023) pages.

styles.era: 8-digit numeric serials (no era dates stated on Luxaire page)
styles.notes: Year first, month second. Same layout as Coleman style-3 but 8 digits and with no era dates stated on the Luxaire page, so no yearFloor override is set.
Month first, year second. Same layout as Coleman style-4 (page text and chart agree on the 9-digit sample here, unlike Coleman's 9/10-digit discrepancy).

TEXT-SOURCED (Phase 2b, not Luxaire-page image-verified): same 4-letter system as Coleman style-2 and York style-2; tables from York-family text decoders, all agreeing; example serial is the Luxaire page's own example. Era '1971-September 2004' is sourced from the sister-system decoders, not from Luxaire page text (which states no era for style 4) — flagged, not hidden. N=2004 is January-September 2004 only. K=September here is the OLD-system value and must not be carried into post-2004 style 1. Building Center chart image read still open for image confirmation.

nordyne.notes: Parent company as stated on the page. The page lists related brands (Broan, Frigidaire, Gibson, Intertherm, Kelvinator, Mammoth, Maytag, Miller, NuTone, Philco, Tappan, Westinghouse, Gaz Industrie, Ambirad, Partners Choice, Reznor and private labels) but does not state they share Nordyne's serial system, so no sisters are claimed. No era dates are documented for either style; eras below describe serial shape only. The two styles do not overlap: style-1 is 12 characters, style-2 is 16 characters.

styles.era: 3-letter prefix followed by 9 digits; year and month encoded
styles.notes: Page example shown as GBB03 0708229. Year is the 4th and 5th positions (03, resolving to 2003 under the 1960 floor); month is the 6th and 7th positions (07 = July). Hyphen variants GBB-030708229 and GBB-0307-08229 normalize to the same serial.

styles.era: 16-character serial with a letter-delimited middle section; week and year encoded, no month
styles.notes: Page example shown as MN3D102 F38 91 4228. Week is the 9th and 10th positions (38, the first two digits after the middle-section letter F); year is the 11th and 12th positions (91, the last two digits of that section, resolving to 1991 under the 1960 floor). The page notes this style is similar to Rheem style serials and likely indicates Rheem manufacture for Nordyne; that similarity is not documented verbatim reuse, so usesStylesOf stays null.

payne.notes: BDP system. Styles 1-4 match Bryant styles 1-4 in shape, positions, era, and example serials (style 2, style 3 and style 4 examples are identical serials on both pages). Payne is NOT usesStylesOf Bryant because Payne style 5 differs from Bryant style 5 and Payne lists no Canada variant for style 3. Styles 3-4 letter/digit tables are transcribed from Bryant page text because Payne's own charts are image-only in text fetch; confirm against Payne chart images before treating those tables as Payne-page-confirmed. HELD GAP — style 5 (prior to 1970, 7-digit all-numeric, year = 1st digit): the page shows only the placeholder 6######, which is not a real serial, and the decade mapping lives only in the chart image; no style 5 is shipped rather than guessed. Carrier is a related brand but its page states no serial system, so it is not claimed as sharing this system.

styles.era: 10-character format, week-year in first four digits
styles.notes: Week is 1st-2nd positions, year is 3rd-4th positions. Week decode for the example is 40.
Year is 1st-2nd positions, month is 3rd-4th positions. Same example serial as Bryant style 2.

Month is 1st position, year digit is 2nd position. Tables transcribed from Bryant page text for the identical BDP system; Payne's own chart is image-only in text fetch. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

Month is 1st position, year digit is 2nd position. Tables transcribed from Bryant page text for the identical BDP system; Payne's own chart is image-only in text fetch. Year uses a digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year.

reznor.notes: PARTIAL YEAR TABLE for style-1, EXTENDED IN PHASE 2b (TEXT-SOURCED): year codes 1995-2029 from Reznor date-code tables in manufacturer documentation (Reznor parts-manual mirror, LDAP manual, date-code chart PDF), three sources agreeing on the sequential pattern (first two letters advance one step per year; third letter A-L is the month, already shipped); BK=2011 matches the Building Center page example. New examples use serials quoted in the source documents themselves, not invented: BLL00000X (manualsdir decoding example, BLL = December 2012) and BOG30600000 (parts-guide sample, BOG = July 2015). Two secondary copies contain obvious typos disregarded here (one duplicates the 2015 BO row for 2017; one prints 'BFID'/'Bill' for 2008 rows; one prints 'BIB' for a 2020 row) — the pattern itself is unaffected. NOT INCLUDED: codes before 1995. Found tables start at 1995 and the Building Center 1949-2029 tables remain unread via text fetch (chart image read still open); extending the sequence backwards arithmetically (1994=AT, ...) is unsourced arithmetic, not a fact, and the pre-1975 code form is unknown (the sequence cannot go below AA in the same form). Pre-1995 stays held pending the browser read. The 2-letter key is the ratified string-keyed table kind (Phase 2b schema). The 2-letter-prefix variant (1-letter year code, per the page tip) is not encoded at all: no year table and no disambiguation rule for it appear in the fetched content, and such serials do not match the style-1 pattern, so they return cannot-determine. Page last updated 2016; parent is as stated on the page.

styles.era: Letter-prefix serials starting with three letters: year is the first two letters, month is the third letter
9-character serials: month is the 1st and 2nd digits, year is the 3rd and 4th digits

rheem.notes: Six documented serial styles. Styles 2-4 share one factory-letter rule (week = 1st and 2nd digits after the factory letter, year = 3rd and 4th digits after it) but are kept as separate styles because the schema positions are absolute and the factory letter sits at a different index in each documented example (index 7, 4, and 5 respectively). Style 5 is described on the page as a common water-heater style also used on some older HVAC systems; style 6 is an older discontinued style from the mid-1970s and prior, also a water-heater style used on older HVAC systems. Example expected values are derived from the page's stated positions (the page states positions, not printed year values); each derived year is the unique candidate under the 1960 floor and 2026 current year. Ambiguity: the factory letter is described as typically F, M, G, W, or N, so a style 2-4 serial with a non-typical factory letter would fall through to style 5 and mis-decode; ordering (styles 2-4 before style 5) protects only the typical-letter cases. Patterns for styles 2-4 anchor the factory-letter position to the documented example's prefix length; a serial with a different prefix length before the factory letter is not covered and must not be guessed.

styles.era: Letter followed by digits; week and year in the opening digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 4th and 5th positions, week = 2nd and 3rd positions. Normalized W291013412: positions 2-3 = 29 (week), positions 4-5 = 10 (year 2010).

styles.era: Seven-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th numbers following the middle (factory) letter, week = 1st and 2nd numbers following it; factory letter typically F, M, G, W, or N. Normalized CB5D302F099903346: factory letter F at index 7, following digits 09 (week) and 99 (year 1999). Example serial shown on the page with a space (CB5D302F09 9903346); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Four-digit prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized 7351M280616735: factory letter M at index 4, following digits 28 (week) and 06 (year 2006). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (7351 M28 06 16735); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Five-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized OR177M280700097: factory letter M at index 5, following digits 28 (week) and 07 (year 2007). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (OR177 M28 07 00097); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Older HVAC systems; month-year opening digits, also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th positions, month = 1st and 2nd positions; common water-heater style also used on some older HVAC systems. Normalized 0804B10488: positions 1-2 = 08 (month August), positions 3-4 = 04 (year 2004). Example serial shown on the page with a space (08 04B10488); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Older discontinued style, mid-1970s and prior; also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = last 2 digits, week = 4th and 3rd from last digits (in that order). Normalized 123451872: last 2 digits 72 (year 1972); 4th from last = 1 and 3rd from last = 8, giving week 18. Example serial shown on the page with a space (1234518 72); normalized form strips the space. Limitation: with the default 1960 floor, a genuine pre-1960 style-6 serial (two-digit year below 60) has no valid candidate under the century rule and returns cannot-determine rather than a guessed year; the page gives no start date that would justify a different floor.

ruud.notes: Reuse evidence (page-confirmed, not parent alone): the Ruud page lists the exact same six example serials as the Rheem page (W291013412; CB5D302F09 9903346; 7351 M28 06 16735; OR177 M28 07 00097; 08 04B10488; 1234518 72), with identical position descriptions for year, month, and week, the identical factory-letter note (typically F, M, G, W, or N), and the identical style images (Rheem-HVAC-style-1.jpg through style-6-1.jpg). The Ruud page also states Rheem Manufacturing acquired Ruud in 1959 and Ruud remains a subsidiary of Rheem Manufacturing. The Rheem page lists many other related brands, but only Ruud is verified here as sharing this serial system; no other related brand is claimed as sharing it.

styles.era: Letter followed by digits; week and year in the opening digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 4th and 5th positions, week = 2nd and 3rd positions. Normalized W291013412: positions 2-3 = 29 (week), positions 4-5 = 10 (year 2010).

styles.era: Seven-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th numbers following the middle (factory) letter, week = 1st and 2nd numbers following it; factory letter typically F, M, G, W, or N. Normalized CB5D302F099903346: factory letter F at index 7, following digits 09 (week) and 99 (year 1999). Example serial shown on the page with a space (CB5D302F09 9903346); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Four-digit prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized 7351M280616735: factory letter M at index 4, following digits 28 (week) and 06 (year 2006). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (7351 M28 06 16735); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Five-character prefix, then factory letter, then week-year digits
styles.notes: Page: same factory-letter rule as style 2; serial may or may not contain spaces. Normalized OR177M280700097: factory letter M at index 5, following digits 28 (week) and 07 (year 2007). Example serial shown on the page with spaces (OR177 M28 07 00097); normalized form strips spaces.

styles.era: Older HVAC systems; month-year opening digits, also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = 3rd and 4th positions, month = 1st and 2nd positions; common water-heater style also used on some older HVAC systems. Normalized 0804B10488: positions 1-2 = 08 (month August), positions 3-4 = 04 (year 2004). Example serial shown on the page with a space (08 04B10488); normalized form strips the space.

styles.era: Older discontinued style, mid-1970s and prior; also a common water-heater style
styles.notes: Page: year = last 2 digits, week = 4th and 3rd from last digits (in that order). Normalized 123451872: last 2 digits 72 (year 1972); 4th from last = 1 and 3rd from last = 8, giving week 18. Example serial shown on the page with a space (1234518 72); normalized form strips the space. Limitation: with the default 1960 floor, a genuine pre-1960 style-6 serial (two-digit year below 60) has no valid candidate under the century rule and returns cannot-determine rather than a guessed year; the page gives no start date that would justify a different floor.

tempstar.notes: ICP system. Sister Keeprite shares styles 1-5 with identical examples and positions, but Keeprite lists no style 6, so no verbatim reuse is claimed in either direction. Style 2 is the same system as style 1 with a printed MFG date on the tag. HELD GAPS — style 4 (8-digit numeric, year = 1st digit, week = 2nd-3rd digits): the format example 30512345 has no stated decode and its year-digit mapping is chart-image-only; styles 5 (letter-digit-letter prefix, year = 3rd letter) and 6 (two-letter prefix, year = 2nd letter): the page shows only placeholders Z3Zxxxxx / ZZxxxxx and the year-letter charts are image-only, and the xxxxx tail shapes are undocumented. None of styles 4-6 is shipped rather than guessed.

styles.notes: Year is 2nd-3rd digits, week is 4th-5th digits. Week decode for the example is 16.

styles.era: Letter followed by 9 digits, with printed MFG date on tag
styles.notes: Page states this serial is identical in system to style 1; the printed MFG date 2/92 corroborates year 1992 and week 06. Pattern and positions duplicate style 1, so this style never wins first-match, but its decode is identical.

styles.era: 10-character format, year-week in first four digits
styles.notes: Year is 1st-2nd digits, week is 3rd-4th digits. Week decode for the example is 14.

trane.notes: Multiple overlapping serial systems; the page advises using data-plate MFR date, ANSI standard date, condition and appearance to disambiguate overlapping styles. Page Style 1 (2002 onward) is documented as used under the Trane, American Standard, Ameristar and Ingersoll Rand names; the page also names GE among brands under which these styles appear. Known-context correction: the page documents the letter-year system from 1983 (not from 1987) through 2001, then the year-first digit system from 2002. Parent per the page header is Ingersoll Rand; the page history notes the 2020 rename to Trane Technologies. HELD, NOT SHIPPED: page Style 7 (8-character serials, documented serial F9190391 with no stated decode; year positions inferred only from similarity to page Style 3) and page Styles 4 (1981-1983, year letter in first or last position depending on product type, ambiguous letter wording), 5 (single-digit year + month letter with no table, decade ambiguous 1970s vs early 1980s), 6 (third-to-last letter year, last two digits week, 1980-1982, no L/M/N letter table), 8 (European; page states it cannot be decoded from any known chart).

styles.notes: Year-prefix range 10-26 in the pattern must be extended as the calendar advances; the century rule alone would misread pre-2010 digit-led serials. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2010+ reading) and style-1 (2002-2009 reading); this style is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading. The page notes the styles overlap and directs techs to the data-plate MFR date to disambiguate; a 2002 serial in the overlap set will decode as a 2020s year.

Single-digit year encoded as a digit-keyed letterTable because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the mapping (digit d = 2000+d for 2002-2009) is the page's stated rule. CAVEAT: the page notes some circa 1978-79 models may have used this shape, so a leading 8 or 9 could be 1978/1979 on a very old unit; condition and appearance disambiguate per the page. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2002-2009 reading) and style-2 (2010+ reading); style-2 is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading and the data-plate MFR date must disambiguate per the page. A 2002 serial in the overlap set therefore decodes as a 2020s year; this is a documented page ambiguity, not a silent guess.

Letter table: the page's chart is an image that text fetch cannot OCR. Anchors confirmed in page text: S = 1986, Z = 2001, F = 1991 (page example F23456789, 23rd week of 1991), C = 1988 (page example C01D47415, 1st week of 1988); header examples are consistent with R = 2000 and M = 1997. Remaining mappings corroborated by independent published Trane charts. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: page text says letters A, I, L, O and Q were not used, yet the standard chart reading (corroborated by three independent sources) gives L = 1996; L = 1996 is included pending visual chart verification. The page warns this style is easily confused with page styles 3, 4, 6 and 7.

styles.era: 1970s onward, factory letter + 2-digit year + month letter, 9 characters (page Style 3)
styles.notes: Page states the 4th position encodes month but gives no letter-to-month table (the documented example's 4th character is M), so month is not encoded. The page warns this style is easily confused with page Style 2; ordering (letter-year style tried first) plus week-range validation resolves most collisions, since a page-Style-3 serial whose factory letter is in the year table and whose year digits are 01-53 would otherwise decode as a letter-year serial.

weil-mclain.notes: Age is decoded from the 7-digit CP number on a separate tag/sticker, NOT from the serial number. Page states the chart is a 'guideline for approximate manufacture year' (1988 into 2023), so every band is approximate:true. Bands 1988-2008 are printed in full and are consecutive with no gaps or overlaps. Bands 2009-2022 are printed with masked xxx endings/beginnings (e.g. 6150xxx); the file expands each xxx prefix to its full 1000-number block, so every CP in a shared-prefix block falls in two bands and must decode to 'cannot determine', never first-match. 2023 device band: the chart prints 2023 as beginning 8067xxx with ending '???', so its entire known range coincides with 2022's ending block; the 8067000-8067999 band for 2023 exists ONLY to force 'cannot determine' on that block, it is not a true 2023 range, and CPs above 8067999 match zero bands (2023 continuation and 2024+ unknown from this chart). Fallback if device bands are rejected: truncate 2022 to max 8066999 and drop 2023. NORMALIZATION (resolved): locked normalization strips spaces, so the prose form 'CP 2530051' normalizes to 'CP2530051'; pattern ^CP\d{7}$ with year positions [2,9] is therefore correct. CAVEATS: AquaBalance model CP numbers are NOT sequential and the chart may not suffice for them (serial alone cannot distinguish them); 6-digit CP numbers are generally early-1980s and prior and the page directs techs to contact Weil-McLain (pattern covers 7-digit only; zero-padded 6-digit values fall below the chart and correctly do not match). Page header misspells parent as 'Marely-Wylain'; history section spelling 'Marley-Wylain' used here. Page header lists Williamson Thermoflo as a related brand; sharing of the CP system is NOT verified, so it is not listed as a sister.

styles.notes: Example CP2530051 is the page's format example (text + data-plate photo, Model GU-4, Series No. 2 — the '2' is a series number, not a year); its year 1993 is chart-derived (2530051 falls in 2400000-2609500), not page-stated. No other example serial appears on the page.

york.notes: Style-1 year uses split-year extraction as an ordered list of half-open ranges [[1,2],[3,4]] whose sliced digits concatenate ('0'+'5'='05') before the century rule; style-2 year uses a dual-candidate letter table whose values are either a single full year (exactly one year) or a two-element candidate list (21-year cycle, both years, never a guessed pick). MONTH CONFLICT RESOLVED FOR YORK: both York charts (style 1 and style 2) map K to September, agreeing with Coleman and with Luxaire's style-4 table; Luxaire's own style-1 chart (K October) remains the sole outlier and is a Luxaire-internal inconsistency, not a York question — York's decode of W0K5896070 is September 2005. No usesStylesOf: York's two styles are defined here in full; Coleman and Luxaire share these two systems (same sample serials, same tables, same October 2004 boundary) but each carries additional numeric styles, so reuse would be wrong in both directions. Parent note: the page names Johnson Controls International as parent and records Bosch's July 2024 agreement to buy the residential/light-commercial HVAC business (sale slated within ~12 months); completion status is not verified on this page (last updated 12/26/2024), so the parent field keeps Johnson Controls International. Quirk: the style-2 data-plate image header reads 'Style 4 Data Plate' although the page text numbers this system Style 2; the plate serial is the same WAKM011379, so this is a legacy image label, not a third style. PARENTHETICAL-PREFIX EDGE, NOT ENCODED: the page cautions that some serials of this style begin with a letter in parentheses, e.g. (S)EBHM062202, meaning 'ignore the first letter in parenthesis' (decodes as EBHM062202: February, 1978 or 1999); the locked normalization strips spaces/dashes only, so that literal input would not match this pattern — left in notes only, deliberately not a formal example, so the builder's every-example-must-decode rule is not broken.

styles.notes: Split-year: 2nd character (index 1) and 4th character (index 3) are the two year digits, split around the month letter; the chart states this explicitly ('The 2nd digit is a 0 and the 4th digit is a 5 ... Combined they read 05 which is equivalent to the year 2005'). Position 0 is the plant letter (chart table: A Apodaca, N Norman, S Source One, W Wichita; not validated by the pattern). Positions 4-9 are a six-digit sequence. Month letters skip I and J. yearFloor 2004 reflects the documented October 2004 start: with this floor, YY=05 resolves to 2005 only and a pre-2004 YY cannot match this style.

21-year cycle, dual-candidate letters A-N (13 letters): first cycle 1971-1991, second cycle 1992-2004, truncated at N=2004 because the style ended October 2004. Single-year letters P-Y (1984-1991) are first-cycle only; their second-cycle years (2005-2012) never occurred under this style, so they decode exactly, never as candidates. Year letters skip I, O, Q, U, Z. Position 0 is the plant letter (chart table: A Addison, B Blackville, C Canada, D Medina, E Elyra, M Madyville, N Norman, W Wichita, X Mexico, Y York). Position 3 is the item type (M Mfg Basic Unit, P Purchased Basic Unit, S Mfg Low Side Item, T Purchased Low Side Item, Y Mfg Accessory, Z Purchased Accessory, O Filler). Positions 4-9 are a six-digit sequence.
